The one-week interval widens considerably, incorporating the cumulative effect of these daily uncertainties alongside potential shifts in short-term sentiment, the release of weekly economic indicators, or minor policy adjustments. These could include unforeseen major economic shocks, such as a sudden recession, a financial crisis, or hyperinflation, which would fundamentally alter the underlying conditions. Geopolitical crises, like unexpected large-scale conflicts, significant trade wars, or widespread political instability, could also trigger extreme market reactions. Furthermore, abrupt and substantial policy changes, such as unexpected interest rate hikes or cuts, dramatic regulatory overhauls, or unprecedented government interventions, could lead to outcomes well outside the predicted range. Lastly, severe natural disasters or new global health crises could disrupt markets and economies in ways that our current probabilistic forecast does not fully capture.
